intent: Step a Carousel forward by one slide, with a fixed chevron icon.
typical_uses: The built-in next-slide control of a Carousel

dont_use_when.situation: A step control with a different look or placement than the fixed chevron button

instead.note: Render a plain Button inside the Carousel and drive it from useCarousel's `scrollNext` and `canScrollNext`.

invariants.text: The button is disabled whenever the engine reports nothing to scroll to in this direction; a consumer `disabled` can only add a reason to disable it and never re-enables it.
A consumer `onClick` is called first and the step forward runs after it on every click; the consumer handler cannot replace the navigation.
Without `aria-label` the button is named "Next slide"; the name is always set, so a caption passed as children does not become the accessible name unless `aria-label` repeats it.

The button is absolutely positioned with its outer edge 3rem beyond the Carousel's box (right of it when horizontal, below it, centred and rotated a quarter turn when vertical), so the surrounding layout has to leave that room.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Place it inside the Carousel it steps; it reads the root's context through useCarousel and throws "useCarousel must be used within a <Carousel />" without one

a11y.by: carousel.test.tsx asserts a button with the accessible name "Next slide" and data-icon-only, and that it is disabled when the engine reports nothing to scroll to

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the next-slide button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the next-slide button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (ButtonState, which carries `disabled`). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and carousel.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Default control, relabelled and restyled
good.code:
<Carousel aria-label="Photos">
  <CarouselContent>
    <CarouselItem>1</CarouselItem>
    <CarouselItem>2</CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselNext aria-label="Show later photo" variant="ghost" size="lg" />
</Carousel>

bad.title: Swapping the glyph through an icon prop
bad.why: CarouselNext takes every Button prop except `icon`; the chevron is fixed.

cannot_extract: default: prop "aria-label" defaults to "Next slide", but the contract states no property for it - the default is not stated

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and carousel.module.css, not through this.
